headline: High: Mentat can read/write shared files and broad network egress can leak Great Expectations outputs; prompt-injection and cascading-error risks are secondary.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Great Expectations reads and writes validation files/documentation, and Mentat reads/writes filesystem content by default. That shared file bridge lets attacker-controlled text in data sources or docs influence Mentat’s instruction parsing. No MCP or clipboard bridge is documented, so I do not escalate to high.
conditions: IF Great Expectations outputs are placed in a directory Mentat reads
IF Mentat treats file contents as instructions or patch context
mitigations: Separate the agents into different working directories
Mark Great Expectations outputs read-only before Mentat runs
Require a human review step for any file Mentat ingests
Use filename allowlists for Mentat input paths
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to generated files

B_data_leakage.rationale: Great Expectations touches validation results and documentation, while Mentat reads selected files and sends prompts to a configured model provider over broad egress. If shared files contain sensitive validation data, Mentat can transmit that context off-host. Great Expectations itself has no network egress, so the leak path is one-way through Mentat.
conditions: IF sensitive validation results are stored in files Mentat reads
IF Mentat forwards those files into its model-provider context
mitigations: Keep sensitive validation outputs out of Mentat’s input directory
Redact secrets before handing files to Mentat
Disable network access for Mentat during sensitive runs
Use a separate non-sensitive workspace for Great Expectations artifacts
requires-engineering: enforce content filtering before API calls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Great Expectations writes validation artifacts and Mentat has write_filesystem plus modify_git_state, with shared state explicitly via filesystem. Both can mutate the same workspace, and Mentat’s git edits can race with Great Expectations outputs. That overlap is dangerous by default because no locking is documented.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same repository or output directory
IF Mentat commits or rewrites files while Great Expectations is generating artifacts
mitigations: Run the agents in separate directories
Serialize access with a simple manual lock file
Pause Mentat while Great Expectations writes outputs
Review git diffs before any commit
requires-engineering: add workspace locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Great Expectations produces validation results that Mentat can read from files and then act on in its diff-based workflow. Because Mentat is designed to propose edits from file context, A’s outputs can become B’s input without a documented verification barrier. That creates a plausible mis-edit cascade, though not an automatic action chain.
conditions: IF Mentat uses Great Expectations reports as authoritative remediation guidance
IF no human verifies the proposed diff against the underlying data
mitigations: Require a human to compare diffs against source data
Limit Mentat to read-only analysis of validation reports
Split validation and remediation into separate review steps
Add a checklist for verifying each suggested fix
requires-engineering: add automated report-to-diff validation

E_compliance.rationale: Great Expectations is documented as touching validation results and documentation, while Mentat handles source code and sends prompts to a configured model provider. The pair does not show a clear residency or regulated-data mismatch in the profiles, but Mentat’s API calls can still create retention/compliance concerns if sensitive validation artifacts are included. The other agent is not cited because no separate compliance boundary is documented for it.
conditions: IF regulated data is included in validation artifacts
IF Mentat forwards those artifacts to a third-party model provider
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from validation files
Review provider retention settings before use
Use synthetic or masked samples for remediation runs
Document which artifacts may leave the host
requires-engineering: add a data-classification gate
